related_questions.question: Is eye discharge a symptom of COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, eye discharge can be a symptom of COVID-19, specifically when the virus infects the conjunctiva, the tissue that covers the white part of the eye and the inside of the eyelids. This can lead to conjunctivitis, also known as pink eye, which may include symptoms like redness, swelling, itching, and eye discharge.

list.title: Conjunctivitis:
list.snippet: When the virus affects the conjunctiva, it can cause inflammation and irritation, leading to symptoms like redness, swelling, and itching.

list.title: Eye discharge:
list.snippet: The discharge can be watery, mucousy, or even crusty, especially in the morning.

list.title: Other eye symptoms:
list.snippet: Other potential eye symptoms include light sensitivity, blurred vision, and pain.

list.title: Seeking medical advice:
list.snippet: If you experience eye pain or vision changes while sick with COVID-19, it's important to consult with an eye doctor (ophthalmologist or optometrist). They can assess the situation and rule out any serious conditions like uveitis or retinal bleeding.
